chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Hafs, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to him, 'Teach me a supplication.' He said, 'So where are you from the supplication of al-ilhah (insistence/urgency)?' I said, 'And what is the supplication of al-ilhah?'

He said: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and what is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, and Lord of Jibra'il, Mikail, and Isra'il, and Lord of the Magnificent Quran, and Lord of Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets. I ask You by that by which the sky is established, and by which the earth is established, and by which You separate the gathered ones, and by which You gather the scattered ones, and by which You provide for the living, and by which You counted the number of sands, and the weight of the mountains, and the measure of the seas.'
Then you send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, then you ask Him for your need, and be insistent in the seeking.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of urgency (Dua al-Ilhah) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication exemplifies the Shia practice of 'Tawassul' by invoking Allah through the cosmic powers of the archangels and the Quran, reflecting the theological emphasis on divine intermediaries. The structure highlights the transition from praising Allah's attributes to sending blessings upon the Ahl al-Bayt, a hallmark of Al-Kulayni's compilation, before presenting the specific need with 'Ilhah' (earnest persistence).

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, fro mIbn Sinan, from Hafs, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Teach me a supplication’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So where are you from the supplication of the urgency?’ I said, ‘And what is the supplication of the urgency?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(say), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the seven skies and what is between these, and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Magnificent Throne, and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>, and Mikaeel<sup>as</sup>, and Israfeel<sup>as</sup>, and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Magnificent Quran, and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, the last of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by which You<sup>azwj</sup> are Regulating the sky, and by which You<sup>azwj</sup> are Regulating the earth, and by it You<sup>azwj</sup> are Separating the gathered ones, and by it You<sup>azwj</sup> are Gathering the separated ones; and by it You<sup>azwj</sup> are Sustaining the living beings, and by it You<sup>azwj</sup> are Counting the grains of sand, and the weight of the mountains, and the measurement of the oceans’.
Then you should send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww. Then you should ask Himazwj your need, and be insistent in the seeking’.
en.sarwar: 23. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ibn Sinan from Hafs from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I asked him to instinct me with a supplication. He asked, ‘Why do you not pray with the supplication of pleading before Allah for help?’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is the supplication of pleading before Allah for help?’

The Imam said say, ‘O Lord, the Lord of the seven heavens and all that is in between, the Lord of the great Throne, Lord of Jibril (Gabriel), Michael and Israfeil, Lord of the great Quran, and Lord of Muhammad, the last of the prophets, I plead before You through that with which You keep the heavens, with which You keep the earth, with which You disperse the gatherings and place together what is scattered, with which You provide sustenance to the living, with which You keep the counts of sands, the weight of the mountains and the measurement of the oceans.’
Then ask Allah’s al-Salat (favor) for Muhammad and his family and ask for help and insist pleading before Allah for help.’”
